question_html: What is the primary motive behind establishing a Not-for-Profit Organisation (NPO)?

options.A: To maximize profits for shareholders and partners
options.B: To render service to the society or the members of the organisation
options.C: To engage in wholesale trading activities for commercial gain
options.D: To distribute dividends among founding members

answer_html: Answer: (B) The main motive behind a non-profitable organisation is to render service to the society or the members of the organisation rather than earning profits[cite: 18].

question_html: A Receipts and Payments Account is essentially a summary of which of the following?

options.A: Profit and Loss Account
options.B: Cash Book without date column

answer_html: Answer: (B) A Receipts and Payments Account is a summary of the cash book without a date column[cite: 18].

question_html: Which financial statement of a Not-for-Profit Organisation is equivalent to the Profit and Loss Account of a profit-making enterprise?

options.A: Receipts and Payments Account
options.B: Income and Expenditure Account

answer_html: Answer: (B) The Income and Expenditure Account is equivalent to the Profit and Loss Account of a profit-making business enterprise[cite: 18].

question_html: In a Not-for-Profit Organisation, an excess of income over expenditure is termed as:

options.A: Net Profit
options.B: Surplus

answer_html: Answer: (B) Profit is termed as Surplus (excess of income over expenditure) in non-profit making organisations[cite: 18].

question_html: What is an excess of expenditure over income called in an NPO?

options.A: Net Loss
options.B: Deficit

answer_html: Answer: (B) Loss is termed as Deficit (excess of expenditure over income) in non-profit making organisations[cite: 18].

question_html: Which of the following principles of accounting is followed in the preparation of an Income and Expenditure Account?

options.A: Cash basis of accounting
options.B: Accrual principle of accounting

answer_html: Answer: (B) The Income and Expenditure Account is prepared by following the accrual principle[cite: 18].

question_html: How are general donations usually treated in the accounts of a Not-for-Profit Organisation?

options.A: Capitalised and added to Capital Fund
options.B: Credited directly to the Income and Expenditure Account
options.D: Credited to a separate liability reserve

answer_html: Answer: (B) General donations are not received for any specific purpose and are shown on the credit side of the Income and Expenditure Account[cite: 18].

question_html: What is the correct accounting treatment for specific donations (e.g., Donation for Building)?

options.A: Credited to Income and Expenditure Account
options.B: Capitalized and shown on the liabilities side of the Balance Sheet

answer_html: Answer: (B) Specific donations received for certain specific purposes should be capitalized and shown on the liabilities side of the Balance Sheet[cite: 18].

question_html: In the absence of any specific instructions or bylaws in the question, how should Entrance Fees be treated?

options.A: Treated as a revenue receipt and credited to Income and Expenditure Account
options.B: Treated as a capital receipt and credited to Capital Fund

answer_html: Answer: (B) If the question is silent, entrance fees should always be taken as a capital receipt and added to the Capital Fund[cite: 18].

question_html: How is Life Membership Fee received by an NPO treated?

options.A: Treated as revenue income
options.B: Capital receipt, added directly to capital fund or general fund

answer_html: Answer: (B) Life Membership Fee is a capital receipt as it is of non-recurring nature and is directly added to the capital fund or general fund[cite: 18].

question_html: What is a Legacy in the context of a Not-for-Profit Organisation?

options.A: An annual subscription paid by regular members
options.B: An amount received by an organization as per the will of a person after death

answer_html: Answer: (B) Legacy is an amount received by an organization as per the will of the person after the death of the person, which should be capitalized[cite: 18].

question_html: How should the proceeds from the sale of old newspapers and periodicals be treated?

options.A: Credited to Capital Fund
options.B: Shown as income on the credit side of the Income and Expenditure Account
options.D: Credited to a special library fund

answer_html: Answer: (B) The amount received on the sale of old newspapers and periodicals is shown as income on the credit side of the Income and Expenditure Account[cite: 18].

question_html: What is 'Honorarium' paid by an NPO?

options.A: Regular monthly salary paid to regular administrative staff
options.B: Token payment made to someone for receiving services from persons who are not regular employees
options.C: Bonus paid to the organization's directors

answer_html: Answer: (B) Honorarium is paid to someone for receiving services from persons who are not employees of the Not for Profit Organisation[cite: 18].

question_html: What does the term 'Capital Fund' represent in a Not-for-Profit Organisation?

options.A: Total share capital contributed by equity shareholders
options.B: Excess of total assets over total outside liabilities
options.D: Total revenue receipts for the year

answer_html: Answer: (B) In not-for-profit organizations, the excess of total assets over total outside liabilities is known as the Capital Fund[cite: 18].

question_html: Which of the following bodies govern educational institutions registered as societies in India?

options.A: Indian Societies Registration Act of 1860
options.B: Banking Regulation Act of 1949

answer_html: Answer: (A) Educational institutions in India are mostly registered as societies under the Indian Societies Registration Act of 1860[cite: 18].

question_html: During 2022, subscription received in cash was ₹42,000, which includes ₹1,600 for 2021 and ₹600 for 2023. Also, ₹3,000 is still outstanding for 2022. What amount should be credited to the Income and Expenditure Account for subscription?
answer_html: Answer: (B) Amount received ($42,000) + outstanding for 2022 ($3,000) - previous year ($1,600) - future advance ($600) = ₹42,800[cite: 18].

question_html: Salaries paid during 2022 were ₹23,000. Salaries unpaid on March 31, 2021 were ₹1,400, prepaid on March 31, 2021 were ₹400, unpaid on March 31, 2022 were ₹1,800, and prepaid on March 31, 2022 were ₹600. What amount should be debited to the Income and Expenditure Account for salaries?
answer_html: Answer: (B) Paid ($23,000) + outstanding at end ($1,800) + prepaid at beginning ($400) - outstanding at beginning ($1,400) - prepaid at end ($600) = ₹23,200[cite: 18].

question_html: Match expenses paid during the year were ₹1,10,000. Match fund as on April 1, 2021 was ₹30,000, donations for match fund received were ₹55,000, and proceeds from sale of match tickets were ₹20,000. How will this be presented in the Balance Sheet?

options.A: Match Fund balance shown as NIL, and excess expenses of ₹5,000 debited to Income and Expenditure Account
options.B: Match Fund shown at ₹5,000 positive liability
options.C: Entire ₹1,10,000 charged to Income and Expenditure Account
options.D: Match fund shown as an asset of ₹5,000

answer_html: Answer: (A) Total fund available = 30,000 + 55,000 + 20,000 = 1,05,000. Since expenses (1,10,000) exceed available fund, fund is reduced to NIL, and remaining ₹5,000 is debited to Income and Expenditure Account[cite: 18].

question_html: A club has 350 members, each paying an annual subscription of ₹1,050. Receipts and Payments Account showed ₹4,10,000 received as subscriptions. Additional info: Subscriptions outstanding on 31.03.2021 was ₹45,000; advance on 31.03.2022 was ₹62,000; advance on 31.03.2021 was ₹30,000. What is the subscription outstanding on 31.03.2022?
answer_html: Answer: (A) Total subscription due for current year = 350 * 1,050 = 3,67,500. Using the subscription account ledger logic, outstanding subscription on 31.03.2022 evaluates to ₹34,500[cite: 18].

question_html: If tournament expenses incurred exceed the tournament fund available, how is the excess treated?

options.A: Shown as an asset in the closing Balance Sheet
options.B: Debited to the Income and Expenditure Account
options.D: Carried forward as a prepaid expense

answer_html: Answer: (B) The excess of expenditure over the tournament fund shall be debited to the Income and Expenditure Account and not taken to the closing balance sheet[cite: 18].

question_html: When preparing opening financial statements for an NPO, how is the opening Capital Fund or Accumulated Fund calculated?

options.A: By summing up all cash receipts of the current year
options.B: By deducting opening liabilities from opening assets
options.C: By taking the closing balance of the Income and Expenditure Account
options.D: By multiplying membership count with annual fee

answer_html: Answer: (B) Opening capital fund or accumulated surplus is calculated by deducting liabilities from assets at the beginning of the year[cite: 18].

question_html: In Republic College, stores selling prices are fixed to give a net profit of 10% on selling price. If college store sales total ₹7,50,000, what is the cost of goods sold (material & supplies consumed) from sales?
answer_html: Answer: (B) Profit is 10% of selling price, so cost is 90% of selling price ($7,50,000 * 90% = ₹6,75,000$)[cite: 18].

question_html: In Smith Library Society, 75% of entrance fees amounting to ₹30,000 is to be capitalized. What amount is credited to the Income and Expenditure Account?
answer_html: Answer: (C) Since 75% ($22,500$) is capitalized, the remaining 25% ($7,500$) is credited to the Income and Expenditure Account[cite: 18].

question_html: If investment in securities is ₹1,50,000 carrying 5% interest p.a., with additional securities of ₹40,000 purchased on October 1, 2021 (accounting year ending March 31, 2022), what is the total interest accrued/earned for the year?
answer_html: Answer: (B) Interest on ₹1,50,000 for full year = ₹7,500. Interest on ₹40,000 for 6 months = ₹1,000. Total interest = ₹8,500[cite: 18].

question_html: For Bombay Medical Aid Society, opening stock of medicine is ₹10,000, medicines purchased during the year equal ₹34,000, and closing stock of medicine is ₹15,000. What is the value of medicine consumed?
answer_html: Answer: (B) Opening stock ($10,000) + Purchases ($34,000) - Closing stock ($15,000) = ₹29,000[cite: 18].

question_html: Which of the following items is recorded on the debit side of a Receipts and Payments Account?

options.A: All cash and bank receipts, whether capital or revenue
options.B: Only revenue receipts pertaining to the current period
options.C: All cash and bank payments, whether capital or revenue

answer_html: Answer: (A) All receipts (capital or revenue) are debited to the Receipts and Payments Account[cite: 18].

question_html: Can surplus or deficit for an accounting period be ascertained directly from a Receipts and Payments Account?

options.A: Yes, easily.
options.B: No, because it shows only cash/bank position and excludes non-cash items and accruals.
options.C: Yes, if capital items are excluded.
options.D: Only if opening cash balance is zero.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Surplus or deficit cannot be ascertained from this account since it shows only cash/bank position and excludes non-cash items[cite: 18].

question_html: What type of account is the Income and Expenditure Account?

options.A: Real Account
options.B: Nominal Account

answer_html: Answer: (B) Being a revenue account prepared to find out surplus or deficit by matching expenses against revenue, it acts as a nominal account[cite: 18].

question_html: Where are subscriptions outstanding at the end of the current accounting period shown in the financial statements?

options.A: Liabilities side of Balance Sheet
options.B: Assets side of Balance Sheet
options.C: Credit side of Income and Expenditure Account
options.D: Debit side of Receipts and Payments Account

answer_html: Answer: (B) The amount of outstanding subscription is adjusted in the subscription account and shown as an asset in the Balance Sheet[cite: 18].

question_html: Where is subscription received in advance for the next accounting period shown?

options.A: Assets side of Balance Sheet
options.B: Liabilities side of Balance Sheet
options.C: Debit side of Income and Expenditure Account
options.D: Credit side of Receipts and Payments Account

answer_html: Answer: (B) Subscriptions received in advance are shown on the liabilities side of the Balance Sheet[cite: 18].

question_html: What is an Endowment Fund Donation?

options.A: A donation where only the income from that donation is to be used for a specific purpose
options.B: A donation used entirely for immediate salaries
options.C: A grant given by the central government for building construction
options.D: A refundable entrance deposit by members

answer_html: Answer: (A) Endowment Fund Donation is received such that only the income from that donation is to be used for a certain specific purpose[cite: 18].

question_html: How is profit or loss on the sale of an old fixed asset treated in an NPO?

options.A: Ignored completely
options.B: Shown in the Income and Expenditure Account
options.C: Credited directly to Receipts and Payments Account

answer_html: Answer: (B) The profit or loss on the sale of a fixed asset is shown in the Income and Expenditure Account[cite: 18].

question_html: Non-profit organizations registered under Section 8 of the Companies Act, 2013 are required to prepare their financial statements as per which schedule?

options.A: Schedule I
options.B: Schedule II

answer_html: Answer: (C) NPOs registered under section 8 of the Companies Act, 2013 must prepare their Income and Expenditure account and Balance Sheet as per Schedule III to the Companies Act, 2013[cite: 18].

question_html: What system of showing donations towards specific purposes separately is termed as?

options.A: Fund accounting
options.B: Cash accounting

answer_html: Answer: (A) This system of showing donations towards specific purposes separately is termed as fund accounting[cite: 18].

question_html: If members have not contributed any capital amount to an NPO, how is the fund balance termed?

options.A: Share Capital Fund
options.B: Accumulated Fund

answer_html: Answer: (B) If members have not contributed any amount, it shall be termed as 'Accumulated fund' instead of 'Capital fund'[cite: 18].

question_html: During the year ended 31st March, 2022, subscriptions received by Jaipur Literary Society were ₹4,50,000, which included ₹20,000 for the year ended 31st March, 2021. Subscriptions due but not received on 31st March, 2022 were ₹15,000. Advance subscription received for 2023 amounted to ₹26,000. Advance subscription received in 2021 included ₹18,000 pertaining to 2021-22. What is the net subscription income for 2021-22?
answer_html: Answer: (B) Based on the subscription ledger calculations, the amount credited to Income from Subscriptions is ₹4,37,000[cite: 18].

question_html: In Sportswriters Club, furniture opening value is ₹9,600 and closing value after 10% depreciation is desired. What is the depreciation amount charged to the Income and Expenditure Account?
answer_html: Answer: (A) Furniture depreciation at 10% on ₹9,600 equals ₹960[cite: 18].

question_html: In Youth Club, subscriptions received during the year based on income and expenditure of ₹7,500, adjusted for opening outstanding of ₹600 (received), advance for 2023 of ₹270, 2022's received in 2021 of ₹450, and 2022's outstanding at end of ₹750, what is the cash received for subscriptions in Receipts and Payments Account?
answer_html: Answer: (B) Following the reverse calculation or Receipts & Payments balancing for subscriptions, cash collected works out to ₹7,170[cite: 18].

question_html: In Republic College, opening stock of stores is ₹3,00,000, purchases of stores & supplies is ₹8,00,000, and closing stock of stores is ₹1,25,000. What is the total material & supplies consumed?
answer_html: Answer: (B) Opening stock ($3,00,000) + Purchases ($8,00,000) - Closing stock ($1,25,000) = ₹9,75,000[cite: 18].

question_html: In Republic College, building original cost is ₹16,00,000 and depreciation rate is 5% on straight-line basis. If opening accumulated depreciation is ₹4,80,000, what is the annual depreciation charged to Income and Expenditure Account and the closing net book value?

options.A: Depreciation ₹80,000; Net Book Value ₹10,40,000
options.B: Depreciation ₹80,000; Net Book Value ₹15,20,000

answer_html: Answer: (A) Annual depreciation = 5% of ₹16,00,000 = ₹80,000. Total accumulated depreciation = 4,80,000 + 80,000 = 5,60,000. Net book value = 16,00,000 - 5,60,000 = ₹10,40,000[cite: 18].

question_html: In Lion Club, cost of asset sold was ₹10,000 (as on 1.4.2021) and sale proceeds were ₹8,000. What is the loss on sale of asset?

options.A: ₹2,000 profit
options.B: ₹2,000 loss

answer_html: Answer: (B) Cost ($10,000) - Sale proceeds ($8,000) = ₹2,000 loss on sale of asset[cite: 18].

question_html: In Lion Club, opening stock of goods was ₹3,80,000, purchases were ₹15,00,000, and closing stock was ₹2,10,000. If operating revenue receipts from coffee room, soft drinks, swimming pool, and tennis court total ₹17,62,000, what is the profit from trading/operations?
answer_html: Answer: (A) Cost of goods sold = 3,80,000 + 15,00,000 - 2,10,000 = 16,70,000. Profit from operations = Total receipts (17,62,000) - Cost of goods sold (16,70,000) = ₹92,000[cite: 18].

question_html: In Sachin Cricket Club, there are 500 members each paying an annual subscription of ₹1,500. Total subscription received during the year was ₹6,45,000 (including ₹12,000 for previous year and ₹18,000 for next year). What is the subscription income to be credited to Income and Expenditure Account?
answer_html: Answer: (B) Total subscription income = Number of members * Annual subscription = 500 * 1,500 = ₹7,50,000[cite: 18].

question_html: For Bombay Medical Aid Society, subscriptions received during the year were ₹50,000. Subscription receivable on 1.1.2022 was ₹1,500, advance on 31.12.2022 was ₹700, receivable on 31.12.2022 was ₹2,200, and advance on 1.1.2022 was ₹1,200. What is the subscription income for the year?
answer_html: Answer: (B) Subscription received ($50,000) - receivable at beginning ($1,500) - advance at end ($700) + receivable at end ($2,200) + advance at beginning ($1,200) = ₹51,200[cite: 18].

question_html: What is the correct treatment of a government grant received by an educational institution for recurring maintenance expenses?

options.A: Treated as a revenue receipt and credited to Income and Expenditure Account
options.B: Credited directly to Capital Fund

answer_html: Answer: (A) Recurring grants in the form of maintenance grants are treated as revenue receipts and credited to the Income and Expenditure Account[cite: 18].

question_html: Which of the following is NOT a feature of a Receipts and Payments Account?

options.A: It is a summary of cash and bank transactions.
options.B: It starts with opening cash/bank balances and ends with closing balances.
options.C: It records only revenue items pertaining to the current accounting period.
options.D: It includes capital as well as revenue transactions.

answer_html: Answer: (C) Receipts and Payments account records both capital and revenue items across past, present, or future periods, so option C describes Income and Expenditure Account, not Receipts and Payments[cite: 18].

question_html: How are laboratory and library deposits collected from students treated by educational institutions?

options.A: Credited to Income and Expenditure Account as tuition fee
options.B: Treated as a liability remaining with the institution until the student finally leaves

answer_html: Answer: (B) Laboratory and library deposits remain with the institution as a liability until the student finally leaves[cite: 18].

question_html: If a fixed asset is acquired out of a specific fund, how should the asset and fund be disclosed?

options.A: Disclosed and accounted for separately under fund-based accounting principles
options.B: Ignored in the balance sheet
options.C: Expensed immediately to Income and Expenditure Account

answer_html: Answer: (A) If any investments or assets are purchased out of a special fund, these are disclosed separately in accordance with fund accounting principles[cite: 18].

question_html: What does the closing balance of a Receipts and Payments Account generally represent?

options.A: Total net profit for the year
options.B: Closing cash in hand and cash at bank balances

answer_html: Answer: (B) The Receipts and Payments account ends with closing cash in hand and cash at bank balances[cite: 18].

question_html: How is the surplus or deficit calculated in the Income and Expenditure Account finally treated in the Balance Sheet?

options.A: Distributed as cash dividends to members
options.B: Added to (if surplus) or deducted from (if deficit) the Capital / Accumulated Fund
options.C: Shown as a separate current liability

answer_html: Answer: (B) The surplus or deficit from the Income and Expenditure Account is added to or deducted from the Capital/Accumulated Fund brought forward from the previous period[cite: 18].
